full_judgment:
Zinat Ara J: This Criminal Appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 30-9-2010 passed by the High Court Division in Criminal Jail Appeal No. 639 of 2006 dismissing the said appeal and thereby affirming the judgment and order dated 11-6-2001 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Barisal in Sessions Case No. 8 of 1995 [Babuganj P.S. Case No. 4(7)92 corresponding to GR No. 41 of 1992] convicting appellant Babul alias Fakrul under section 302 of the Penal Code, 1860 (shortly, the Penal Code) and sentencing him to suffer imprisonment for life and also to pay a fine of Taka 5,000 (five thousand), in default, to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 2 (two) years more. 

 Prosecution case 

 2. The prosecution case, in short, are that one Rahima Begum, as informant, lodged First Information Report (the FIR) at Babuganj Police Station on 15-7-1992 stating that on 14-7-1992 her younger brother Chande Ali told her that he would go to Moidaner hat to invite their house, the Government Surveyors, who had been in the said "Char". The informant had gone to Donerkandi and while she was returning back home therefrom one Kanchon informed her that her brother Chande Ali was kidnapped by some party persons. Then she went to Kalikapur to search his brother and came to know that his brother (the deceased) was being brought back by Azhar in injured condition by boat. After arrival of the boat, she took her brother by boat to the doctor, who declared him dead. Thereafter, the informant came to the Police Station with the dead body of his brother and lodged the FIR stating the said facts and suspecting Shadek Kha, who had land dispute with his brother, might have killed him. Priya Lal, Prince and Rezaul Karim were also suspected in the FIR in the murder of Chande Ali. 

 3. On receiving the FIR, the police recorded Babuganj PS Case No. 04 dated 15-7-1992 under section 302 of the Penal Code, prepared inquest report on examining the dead body of deceased Chande Ali on 15-7-1992 at 6-00 am in presence of the witnesses, sent the dead body to the hospital morgue for autopsy and it was done on the same day. Thereafter, the police investigated into the case and submitted charge-sheet No. 47 dated 15-12-1992 against the sole convict-appellant under section 302 of the Penal Code. Subsequently, a supplementary charge-sheet being charge-sheet No. 40 dated 18-7-1996 was also submitted by the police against 6 (six) other accused persons i.e. totally 7 (seven) persons including the convict-appellant. 

 4. The case was sent for trial to the Court of Sessions Judge, Barisal and was numbered as Sessions Case No. 08 of 1995. The said case was transferred to the 1st Court of Additional Sessions Judge, Barisal (hereinafter mentioned as the trial court). Charge was framed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Barisal under section 302 read with section 34 of the Penal Code against the accused persons including the convict-appellant, the accused present pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. 

 5. The prosecution examined fourteen witnesses in support of the prosecution case, some of whom where cross-examined by the defence. 

 7. It be mentioned that convict-appellant Babul alias Fakrul was arrested by the police and then obtained bail in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 335 of 1997 and thereafter, he was all along absconding and did not appear before the trial court. So, a State Defence counsel was appointed for his defence (vide judgment of the trial court). 

 10. Feeling aggrieved by the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division the convict-appellant filed Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 289 of 2014 for granting leave to appeal against the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division. This Division, upon hearing, granted leave to appeal on the submissions of Mr SM Shahjahan, the learned Advocate for the convict-appellant that the case was of no evidence so far as it relates to the convict-appellant in view of the facts that none of the prosecution witnesses said anything involving the convict-appellant about the occurrence and, therefore, the High Court Division erred in law in upholding the judgment and order of conviction and sentence passed by the trial court. 

 11. Mr SM Shahjahan, the learned Advocate appearing for the convict-appellant takes us through the FIR, the statements of the prosecution witnesses and submits that none of the prosecution witnesses stated that convict-appellant caused the death of deceased Chande Ali. He next submits that the appellant is neither named in the FIR nor there was any eye witness to support the prosecution case about causing death of deceased Chande Ali by the appellant. He also submits that the witnesses including the informant did not mention anywhere from whom they have heard that Babul alias Fakrul murdered the deceased. He further submits that it is a case of no evidence against the appellant but the trial court committed an error of law in finding the appellant guilty of the charge levelled against him under section 302 of the Penal Code and convicting and sentencing him thereunder. He next submits that the High Court Division without considering the evidence on record erroneously affirmed the judgment and order of conviction and sentence of the trial court. He finally submits that in the above facts and circumstances, the judgment of the trial court as well as the High Court Division is liable to be set-aside and the convict-appellant is liable to be acquitted from the charge under section 302 of the Penal Code by allowing the appeal. 

 12. In reply, Mr Biswajit Debnath, the learned Deputy Attorney-General also takes us through the evidence on record and submits that the accused after obtaining bail absconded and did not surrender throughout the trial and long abscondence of the accused is a circumstance which proves that he has committed the offence under section 302 of the Penal Code. He, by inviting our attention to the statements of PWs 1-2 and also the medical evidence and submits that it is true that there was no eye witness in this case and that one or two witnesses, who mentioned the names of the convict-appellant, did not mention that they recognized the convict-appellant at the time of murdering the deceased and they did not also mention wherefrom they heard the name of the convict-appellant but the circumstances clearly show that the witnesses did not disclose the entire facts out of fear and that some of the witnesses were also declared hostile by the prosecution. He lastly submits that in the facts and circumstances, considering the circumstantial evidence, the order of conviction and sentence of the appellant is justified and the appeal ought to be dismissed. 

 16. PW 10, Uttam Kumar is the recording officer and part investigating officer of the case. PW 12, Nikhil Chandra Mondal is also an investigating officer. PW 7, Dr. Abdul Barek hold post mortem examination on the dead body. So, they are official witnesses of the case and they have not witnessed the incident. 

 18. On examination of the entire evidence on record, it transpires that no eye witness was examined by the prosecution showing that the convict-appellant murdered deceased Chande Ali. The appellant did not make any confessional statement about the murder of the deceased. Some of the witnesses were declared hostile by the prosecution. It is true that the accused after obtaining bail absconded but merely because of abscondence of the accused without any other incriminating direct or convincing Circumstantial evidence against him, he cannot be convicted. It appears that the order of conviction and sentence passed by the trial court against the accused appellant is practically on the basis of hearsay evidence of few witnesses, which is not admissible evidence, in absence of the eye witness to support the prosecution case. 

 22. The judgment and order dated 30-9-2010 passed by the High Court Division in Criminal Jail Appeal No. 639 of 2006 dismissing the said appeal and thereby affirming the judgment and order of conviction and sentence dated 11-6-2001 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Barisal in Sessions Case No.8 of 1995 is hereby set-aside and the convict-appellant is acquitted of the charge under section 302 of the Penal Code. 

 23. The convict-appellant be set at liberty at once, if not wanted in connection with any other case.
